newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to start repatriating Guatemalan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to start repatriating Guatemalan refugees.

text.p: Mexico said on Friday it would begin the voluntary repatriation of 2,790 Guatemalan refugees from its southeastern states in two weeks' time and more would be sent back in the coming months.
Up to 30,000 Guatemalans have sought refuge in Mexico over the past 15 years, escaping massacres and widespread repression during Guatemala's 36-year civil war.
However a peace agreement signed on Dec. 29 brought an end to the conflict between the government and left-wing rebels.

The Mexican government said in a statement it would begin repatriating the refugees on July 4 as part of the measures agreed under a tripartite pact signed by Mexico, Guatemala and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Refugees in the southern Mexican states of Chiapas, Campeche and Quintana Roos would be repatriated as of July 15, it added.
The Guatemalan government has set aside 17,300 acres (7,000 hectares) to settle 558 refugee families and would buy more land to encourage the return of 42 more refugee groups, the statement said.
